analysis:
The PR change in MiMoV26NativeLoadTransaction.swift is small. It adds a private `mediaReservationRemovalHookForTesting` property (head line 299), and rewrites `removeSettledMediaReservation` (head ~1097-1109) so it removes the settled reservation under the lock and then calls the optional test hook outside the lock. A new `setMediaReservationRemovalHookForTesting` setter is added.

Security-relevant behavior:
- Removal still requires `reservation.isFullyRetired` and an identity match (`===`) in `mediaReservations`. The removal guard and the lock scope are unchanged in substance. The new guard returns nil early if the entry is absent or has been replaced, which is equivalent to the old `if` check.
- The hook runs outside `lock`, so it cannot create a lock-order inversion with registry -> transaction -> permit/ledger. A hook that re-enters the transaction cannot deadlock.
- The hook is an internal (not private) method with no production caller visible in the supplied evidence. It is not gated by `#if DEBUG`. It is observation-only (`() -> Void`) and receives no reservation, key or prompt data. Setting it needs in-process code access, which is already inside the attested process boundary (TB-003/T-013). Even a malicious hook cannot change ledger charges, since the reservation is already retired.
- Nothing here touches the A-001 prompt data path, the coordinator wire, encryption, attestation, authorization (T-053), or the prefix cache (T-041). The memory-ledger accounting for media reservations is unchanged: the `mediaReservations` removal semantics are preserved.

Remaining questions for integration: confirm that the testing hook is not invoked or set from production code, and that callers of `removeSettledMediaReservation` (the retire closure ~line 975 and the host-completion closure ~line 1080) still behave correctly. Those callers are unchanged and not re-examined beyond the visible text. The text was truncated at line 1083, so the rest of the file was not reviewed. No regression identified.
